title: Data plane: add KMS client circuit breaker + standardized retry/backoff policy
author: Emily Zhao
description:
Summary: Introduces a circuit breaker around KMS Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey calls in the data plane, plus a single standardized retry/backoff policy used across AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault client adapters. This is intended to reduce cascading failures during partial KMS brownouts (timeouts/throttling) and to make failure modes predictable for SRE runbooks and game days.

Motivation: We have seen intermittent KMS dependency degradation cause request amplification (per-token paths triggering repeated decrypt attempts) and uneven behavior across providers (different retry defaults, different handling of throttling). This PR adds a consistent policy: bounded retries with jittered exponential backoff, plus a breaker that opens on sustained dependency errors to protect the rest of the serving stack.

Key behavior: (1) Retry policy: retry only on explicitly transient classes (timeouts, throttling/429, 5xx, connection resets) with max attempts capped. Do not retry on AccessDenied/InvalidKey/NotFound/etc. (2) Circuit breaker: per-tenant+provider+key-id bucketed breaker (to avoid a single noisy tenant forcing global open). Breaker opens after a configurable failure-rate threshold over a rolling window. When open, calls fail fast with a typed error and emit structured metrics. (3) Cache interplay: breaker does not affect DEK cache hits; only wraps outbound KMS RPC. (4) Observability: emits metrics for breaker state transitions and retry counts; logs are sampled to avoid noise.

Config/flags: Adds runtime flags under kms_client.* (all default OFF / conservative for initial rollout): kms_client.retry.max_attempts (default 3), kms_client.retry.base_backoff_ms (default 50), kms_client.retry.max_backoff_ms (default 750), kms_client.retry.jitter (default true), kms_client.breaker.enabled (default false), kms_client.breaker.window_seconds (default 30), kms_client.breaker.min_requests (default 20), kms_client.breaker.failure_rate_to_open (default 0.5), kms_client.breaker.open_duration_seconds (default 20). Provider overrides are supported (e.g., kms_client.aws.breaker.*).

Rollout notes: Plan is to enable retries first (breaker disabled) in staging, then enable breaker for a small canary tenant set in Hosted, followed by Dedicated. Private remains opt-in via values.yaml / installer config until we publish the operator docs and run the game day. This PR intentionally fails fast when breaker is open; callers should rely on cache where possible and surface a clear error upstream.

Test plan: Unit tests cover retry classification, jitter bounds, breaker open/half-open/closed transitions, and provider adapter mapping of errors -> typed transient/permanent categories. Also includes a deterministic fake clock to avoid flakiness.

Follow-ups: (a) Add alerting thresholds and dashboards wired to the new metrics (ENG-4239). (b) Expand failure-injection harness usage in staging once the hooks land (separate PR). (c) Ensure runbook references the new toggles for rapid mitigation.

Risk: Medium. Changes are gated behind flags but touch a common KMS wrapper used by encryption paths. Main risk is aggressive breaker settings causing self-inflicted fail-fast during small blips; defaults are conservative and breaker is disabled by default.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Metrics emitted - [x] Flags documented in config reference - [x] Rollout plan captured in PR description - [x] Reviewed with Security + SRE
commits: kms: add typed error taxonomy (transient vs permanent) and mapping helpers
kms: implement jittered exponential backoff retry policy (shared)
kms: introduce per-tenant circuit breaker wrapper for KMS calls
config: add kms_client.* flags and provider override plumbing
tests: add fake clock + unit tests for retry/breaker logic
obs: add metrics for retry counts, breaker state, and fast-fail errors
docs: inline comments + config reference updates
review_thread:
Vikram Singh (review): The per-tenant breaker bucket key includes key-id; can you confirm we won't explode cardinality on metrics if key-id is high-variance? Also, please ensure this wrapper is not on the hot-path when cache hits.

Emily Zhao (author): Good call. Metrics do NOT tag raw key-id; they tag provider + tenant + operation + breaker_state only. The breaker bucket uses key-id internally but is bounded by an LRU (max_buckets=2k per process, configurable). Also confirmed in profiling: for cache hits we don't call into this wrapper at all; only wraps outbound RPC.

Marcus Lin (review): Retry classification: please double-check AccessDeniedException and InvalidCiphertextException are treated as permanent (no retries). Also would like a single typed error surfaced upstream so audit events can attach stable reason codes later.

Emily Zhao (author): Updated mapping: AccessDenied/InvalidCiphertext/NotFound/DisabledKey => permanent, no retries. Added KmsDependencyError{Reason, ProviderCode, Retryable} wrapper so callers can uniformly report. (Audit events will be in a separate PR but this should unblock it.)

Sean Gallagher (review): Circuit breaker defaults: window=30s and min_requests=20 feels fine, but open_duration=20s might be too short if KMS is hard down and we flap between half-open attempts. Could we increase open_duration and add half-open max probes?

Emily Zhao (author): Implemented half-open with max_probes=3 per open cycle and added kms_client.breaker.half_open_max_probes flag (default 3). Also increased default open_duration to 20s but we can tune during canary; breaker stays disabled by default.

Allison Grant (review): Metrics naming: please align with our conventions (kms_client_*). Also add a counter for fast-fail due to breaker open vs genuine provider failures.

Emily Zhao (author): Done: kms_client_requests_total{result=success|error|fast_fail}, kms_client_retry_attempts_total, kms_client_breaker_state{state=0|1|2}, kms_client_breaker_transitions_total{from,to}. Added fast_fail as distinct result.

Vikram Singh (follow-up): Can you add a short comment on why we retry GenerateDataKey but not Decrypt in some cases? I’m worried about silent latency spikes on decrypt.

Emily Zhao (author): Added note + behavior: we retry Decrypt only for transient transport/throttle errors; we do not retry on InvalidCiphertext or AccessDenied. Retries are capped at 3 total attempts and max_backoff is 750ms; with streaming workloads this stays within our dependency budget. Also added metric to track p95 dependency latency impact in the dashboard follow-up.

Marcus Lin (approval): Looks good with the permanent error mapping and typed wrapper.

Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved; please coordinate with Connor on flag rollout so on-call knows the toggles.

Allison Grant (approval): Approved after metrics rename.
release_notes: Adds standardized KMS retry/backoff policy (timeouts/throttling/5xx only).
Introduces optional KMS circuit breaker to fail fast during dependency brownouts (default disabled).
Adds metrics for KMS retries and breaker state transitions to support alerting/runbooks.
